title: You Think This Pagoda Is 1,000 Years Old — The Real One Fell in 1924 | China Travel Expert
description:
The Leifeng Pagoda is one of the famous sights of Hangzhou's West Lake — and most visitors assume they're looking at something a thousand years old. They aren't.

The original pagoda was built in 975, in the final days of the Wuyue Kingdom. Over the centuries locals chipped and dug bricks out of its base — some believed the bricks brought luck or warded off illness — and on 25 September 1924 the weakened tower simply collapsed. For most of the 20th century the site was just a pile of ruins.

The golden-topped pagoda you photograph today opened in October 2002: a steel-and-concrete tower rebuilt directly over the old foundations, with the preserved ruins of the original on display underneath.

Ancient site, modern tower — does it still count as "ancient"? Tell me where you land.

★ Expert Tip: go up the escalators at dusk — the pagoda frames West Lake and the city lights, and the ground floor lets you see the real 10th-century ruins under glass.

雷峰塔原建于 975 年，1924 年因砖石被挖、塔身年久失修而倒塌；如今这座金顶塔是 2002 年在旧址上重建的钢混新塔，底层保留着原塔遗址。古迹还是新塔？
